title: China Travel Guide
summary: A practical guide to China for first-time travellers, covering top cities, visa planning, seasonal highlights, and cultural dos and don'ts.
bestTime: April–May and September–October for mild weather and comfortable sightseeing.

quickFacts.Language: Mandarin Chinese; English is common in major cities.
quickFacts.Visa: China Tourist visa required; e-visa available for some nationalities through official channels.
quickFacts.Transport: High-speed rail is efficient between major cities; domestic flights cover longer distances.

attractions.name: Great Wall
attractions.summary: A world-famous wonder stretching across northern China with scenic and historic sections to explore.

attractions.name: Beijing
attractions.summary: China’s capital blends imperial history, modern architecture, and world-class museums.

attractions.name: Shanghai
attractions.summary: A futuristic skyline, vibrant food scene, and historic riverside Bund district.

attractions.name: Xi'an
attractions.summary: Home of the Terracotta Army and a rich gateway to ancient Silk Road history.

attractions.name: Guilin & Yangshuo
attractions.summary: Limestone karst landscapes, river cruises, and peaceful countryside scenery.

cultureEtiquette: Learn basic greetings and avoid loud behaviour in public spaces.
Respect queues, especially at train stations and tourist sites.
Use both hands for giving and receiving items to show courtesy.
gettingAround: Use China’s high-speed train network for fast intercity travel.
Book taxis via apps like DiDi in major cities for convenience.
Download offline maps and translation apps before travel.
sustainability: Choose trains instead of flights where possible.
Carry a reusable water bottle and use drink stations.
Follow local recycling guidance and minimise plastic waste.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for China?
faqs.a: Yes, most travellers require a tourist visa; apply through the official Chinese visa service before departure.

faqs.q: What is the best route for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: A Beijing-Shanghai-Xi'an route offers a strong mix of history, culture, and modern China.

faqs.q: Can I use my phone data easily?
faqs.a: Buy a local SIM or global roaming plan and use offline maps and translation apps for backup.
